column2: What does the “Read → Fix → Spot → Add” strip of the workshop mean?
column3: At the top of the right-hand panel of the 📜 Transcription workshop, four steps: Read (“✨ Read ▾” or type the text), Fix (suggested corrections, doubtful words [?], “📖 Reading help”), Spot (“🧭 Spot” the names, dates and places), Add (“✓ Add to the family tree…”). The current step is blue, a finished step ticks itself in green, and under each one you read what is left: “7 lines”, “2 words to check”, “3 to link”. Clicking a step brings its buttons forward; “Next step ›” moves on. “✓ Add to the family tree…” always stays at the bottom of the panel.

column2: How do I check a transcription line by line, with the image above?
column3: “👁 Check line by line” (Fix step, Display menu, or the R key) opens the workshop in full screen: the piece of image for the line (its area) right above the line of text. You fix it on the spot: the text of the record follows. Enter: the line is checked, on to the next one; ⇧ Enter: previous line; ↑ ↓: change line without marking it; “↶ Undo” puts the line back as it was; Esc closes. Checked lines are kept with the record. It needs one area per line (placed by the reading, or drawn with ▭). This mode can be turned off in Settings → “📜 Transcription workshop” (recommended: on).

column2: How do I go back to yesterday’s text of a record, or fix a name everywhere?
column3: File → “🕘 Versions…”: a version is kept at each save where the text changed, and just before big changes (“Replace all”, sure suggestions accepted, a reading put into the text). You see each version, compare it word by word with now, and “↺ Go back” restores it (the current text is kept first; “↶ Undo” right after). To fix a misread name everywhere: ⌘F searches the text (results highlighted, Enter / ⇧ Enter), ⌥⌘F adds “Replace” and “Replace all” (the areas follow; “↶ Undo”). ⌘/ shows all the keys of the workshop.

column2: How do I know how far I am in a transcription?
column3: Under the strip of the 📜 Transcription workshop, a progress line: the status of the record (To do, In progress, Checked, Finished: one click to change it), the doubtful words, the checked lines (“5 / 7 lines checked”), the lines linked to their area and the people to link. Clicking a counter goes to the first place concerned: the next [?], the line without an area, the first line not checked. When everything is checked with no doubtful word, the workshop offers “✓ Mark as checked”, and when everything is at zero “✓ Mark as finished”, never on its own. The “Record transcriptions” list shows and filters these statuses.

column2: What do the words underlined with dots in the workshop mean?
column3: They are abbreviations known to “📖 Reading help”: labr, Vve, led., dud., 7bre, inh.… (in French, and in the language of the text chosen in “✨ Read ▾”). Move the mouse over one (or tap the word): a bubble gives the full form (“7bre = September”) and “Open in 📖 Reading help” to learn more. The text does not change: you transcribe as written. Display → “Stop underlining abbreviations” hides them; the setting is also in Settings (recommended: underlined).

column2: How do I transcribe a record on a phone?
column3: On a small screen, the 📜 Transcription workshop shows three tabs at the top: 🖼️ Image (the image in large, its areas, “🎚️ See better” and the zoom), 📝 Text (the strip, the characters, the text and “✓ Add to the family tree…” at the bottom) and 👥 People (with their number: the people of the record, what the app found, and the record sheet: kind, date, place, source, status). One tab at a time, in large; “show in the text” switches to the Text tab by itself. Line-by-line checking also works on a phone.
